questions.question: In India, the ______ may create and dissolve any of the union territories, whose powers are more limited than those of the states.

__
 
• **In India, the Union Government has the power to create and dissolve union territories.**
 
• Union territories are **administrative divisions of India that are governed by the Union Government, either in part or in whole.**
 
• Their** powers are more limited than those of the states, which are self-governing and have their own governments. **
 
• The Union Government also has the power to: create new states, combine states, change state boundaries, and terminate a state's existence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Chief Justice also acts as the president of India if the offices of both the president and vice president are vacant. 
 
 
 
• **President**
 
 
• The **President of India is the head of state and commander-in-chief of the Indian Armed Forces.**
 
• The President's Secretariat assists the President in carrying out their constitutional, ceremonial, and other state responsibilities. 
 
 
 
• **State Governmen**t
 
 
• The Chief Secretary leads the State Government to the state government.

questions.question: 'Matho Nagrang' is associated with which of the following states/UTs?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ladakh**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• "Matho Nagrang" is a traditional religious festival celebrated at **Matho Monastery**, which is located in the **Ladakh region** of India.
 
• It is one of the most important and colorful festivals in Ladakh, celebrated by the local Buddhist community, primarily the **Lama (monk) sect** of the region.
 
• The festival is held annually in **February or March**, usually during the **14th and 15th day of the first month** of the Tibetan lunar calendar.
 
• One of the main highlights of the festival is the **mask dance** performed by the monks of the Matho Monastery.
 
• The dancers wear traditional costumes and masks, representing various deities and religious figures, performing intricate dances to invoke blessings and ensure prosperity for the community
 
• During the festival, **two oracles** (monks who are believed to possess spiritual powers) are chosen to enter into a trance.
 
• These oracles communicate divine messages and predictions during the festival, which are considered highly significant by the local people.

questions.question: The X-ring on the archery target is the ______ inner ring.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**10th**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **X-ring** on an archery target is the **inner ring of the 10th scoring zone**.
 
• It is the highest-scoring area, placed at the center of the target and is used to determine if an arrow lands in the **perfect 10-point zone**.
 
• The X-ring helps to distinguish between two arrows that are both in the 10-point zone but may not be in exactly the same position.
 
• The **innermost ring** (at the center) represents the **highest score** of **10 points**.
 
• The rings surrounding this central area represent scores progressively lower than 10, ending with the **outermost ring**, which is worth **1 point**.

questions.question:
Read the following about the Green Revolution in India.

A. The Green Revolution in India is largely the Wheat Revolution as the wheat production increased by more than three times between 1967-68 and 2003-04, while the overall increase in the production of cereals was only two times B. It resulted in a grain output of 131 million tonnes in the year 1978-79 and established India as one of the world's biggest agricultural producers.

Identify the CORRECT statement/statements.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and B**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Statement A:**

 
 
• "The **Green Revolution in India is largely the Wheat Revolution **as the wheat production increased by more than three times between 1967-68 and 2003-04, while the overall increase in the production of cereals was only two times."
 
• **This statement is correct in the context of wheat.**
 
• The Green Revolution did have a significant impact on wheat production in India, especially after the introduction of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, modern irrigation techniques, and better farming practices.
 
• **Between 1967-68 and 2003-04, wheat production increased substantially, and indeed, wheat played a prominent role in the Green Revolution.**
 
• However, the growth in the overall cereal production was not as dramatic as in wheat, which supports this part of the statement.
 
 
 
• **Statement B**:
 
 
• "**It resulted in a grain output of 131 million tonnes in the year 1978-79 and established India as one of the world's biggest agricultural producers."**
 
• This **statement is correct as well.**
 
• The Green Revolution led to a significant increase in food grain production, and by 1978-79, India achieved a record grain output of around 131 million tonnes.
 
• **This surge in production helped India move towards food self-sufficiency and made it one of the largest agricultural producers in the world.**

questions.question: Fundamental Rights are contained in ______ of the Constitution of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Part III**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Fundamental Rights are contained in **Part III** of the Constitution of India.
 
• These** rights are guaranteed to all citizens and are a cornerstone of the Indian Constitution, ensuring basic freedoms and protections for individuals.**
 
• **Part III consists of Articles 12 to 35 **and covers a range of rights such as the right to equality, the right to freedom, the right against exploitation, the right to freedom of religion, cultural and educational rights, and the right to constitutional remedies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Part IX - The Panchayats**:

 
 
• **Part IX of the Constitution of India deals with the Panchayats, which are the rural local government bodies.**
 
• It** includes provisions related to the structure**, functioning, and powers of Panchayats at various levels (village, intermediate, and district levels).
 
• **This part was added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992**.
 
• The aim is to promote decentralization of power and ensure local self-governance.
 
 
 
• **Part X - The Scheduled and Tribal Areas**:
 
 
• **Part X of the Constitution deals with Scheduled and Tribal Areas (Articles 244 to 244A).**
 
• It **provides special provisions for the administration of regions with a significant tribal population, particularly in North-East India and other tribal areas.**
 
• The provisions are meant to protect the rights and cultural identity of tribal communities and ensure their social and economic welfare.
 
 
 
• **Part XI - Relations between the Union and States:**
 
 
• **Part XI of the Constitution deals with the distribution of legislative, executive, and financial powers between the Union and State governments (Articles 245 to 263).**
 
• It **specifies the areas where the Union Parliament can legislate and where the State Legislatures have jurisdiction.**
 
• It also contains provisions on the disputes between Union and States and the control of the Union over State matters in certain situations.

questions.question: The Iron Age in India is associated with the _______ period, which lasted from about 1500 to 500 BCE.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vedic**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Iron Age** in India is associated with the **Vedic** period, which lasted from about **1500 to 500 BCE**.
 
• The **Vedic period** marks the time when iron tools and weapons began to be widely used in India.
 
• This period is named after the **Vedas**, which are the oldest sacred texts of Hinduism, composed during this time.
 
• The use of iron significantly transformed agriculture, warfare, and society during this era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **British Period:**

 
 
• The **British period refers to the time when India was under British colonial rule, from the mid-18th century (starting after the Battle of Plassey in 1757) until India's independence in 1947.**
 
• During this period, significant changes took place in India, including the establishment of the British Raj, the development of infrastructure like railways, and the introduction of modern education and legal systems.
 
• The Iron Age is not associated with the British period; this era occurred much earlier.
 
 
 
• **Mauryan Period:**
 
 
• The **Mauryan period (around 322-185 BCE) was marked by the rise of the Maurya Empire, founded by Chandragupta Maurya. **This was one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• The Mauryan Empire is significant for its political organization, its spread of Buddhism under Ashoka, and the establishment of a centralized administration.
 
 
 
• **Mughal Period:**
 
 
• The **Mughal period refers to the time when the Mughal Empire ruled India, from 1526 (with the first battle of Panipat) until the mid-19th century** (with the British consolidating control after the Indian Rebellion of 1857).
 
• **This period is known for its monumental architecture (like the Taj Mahal), the flourishing of art and culture, and the establishment of a centralized empire.**

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a government budget in a country's economy?
questions.solution:

• The **primary purpose of a government budget** is to plan and allocate resources efficiently to meet the economic and social needs of the country. 
 
• This involves:
 
 
• **Revenue and expenditure planning:** Ensuring the government has enough resources to finance public goods and services.
 
• **Economic stability:** Managing inflation and economic growth through fiscal policy.
 
• **Redistribution of income:** Addressing inequalities through taxation and welfare programs.
 
• **Resource allocation:** Prioritizing sectors like health, education, defense, and infrastructure.

questions.question: With respect to the Anusandhan National Research Foundation Bill, 2023, who will audit the accounts of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation annually?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CAG**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India will audit the accounts of the Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) annually.
 
• The foundation will also pay the CAG for the audit-related expenses.
 
• The CAG will submit a report on the audit to Parliament. 
 
• The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Bill, 2023 was passed by the Lok Sabha on August 7, 2023.
 
• The bill establishes the NRF and details its finances.
 
• The central government will also prescribe rules for how the funds are used.
 
• The NRF will have a Governing Board, led by the Prime Minister, that will monitor the foundation's implementation and provide strategic direction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• External Affairs Minister
 
 
• The External Affairs Minister (EAM) of India is responsible for representing the country in international relations, diplomacy, and foreign policy matters.
 
• Key Responsibilities:
 
• Overseeing India's foreign policy and international affairs.
 
• Participating in diplomatic engagements, treaties, and agreements.
 
• Representing India at international organizations like the United Nations.
 
 
 
• Finance Commissioner
 
 
• Role: This is not a central role in India's government structure. However, the term "Finance Commissioner" can refer to:
 
• Officials responsible for overseeing financial matters within a state's administrative framework.
 
• At the central level, the Finance Commission is a constitutional body tasked with recommending the distribution of financial resources between the Union and the states.
 
 
 
• Central Vigilance Commissioner (CVC)
 
 
• The CVC is the head of the Central Vigilance Commission, an independent body tasked with combating corruption in the Indian government.
 
• Key Responsibilities:
 
• Overseeing investigations into corruption cases in central government departments.
 
• Advising the government on corruption-related matters.
 
• Monitoring the functioning of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in corruption cases.

questions.question: India's population pyramid, with a wide base and narrower top, suggests what type of population structure?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Expansive**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• I**ndia's population pyramid**, with a wide base and narrower top, suggests an expansive population structure
 
• A **population pyramid with a wide base and narrow top is called an expansive pyramid, and it indicates a growing population.**
 
• This is **because a large percentage of the population is in the younger age groups, which is a sign of high birth rates.**
 
• The **narrow top indicates high death rates and lower life expectancies. **
 
• **Expansive pyramids **are common in developing countries.
 
• India is an example of a country with an expansive population pyramid. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other types of population pyramids include**:

 
 
• **Constrictive:** A pyramid with a narrow base indicates declining birth rates.
 
• **Stationary: **A pyramid with a somewhat equal proportion of the population in each age group.

questions.question: In the first phase of the Green Revolution, which states primarily benefited from the use of HYV seeds?

options.text: Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **During the first phase of the Green Revolution,** the states that primarily benefited from the use of HYV seeds were Punjab, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu: 
 
• The **Green Revolution was a period of agricultural** reform that introduced new farming techniques and high-yielding varieties (HYV) of seeds to increase crop yields and food security.
 
• **The first phase of the Green Revolution took place from the mid-1960s to the mid-1970s.**
 
• During this time, **HYV seeds were primarily used in wheat-growing regions of more affluent states.** 
 
• **HYV seeds require a lot of water, f**ertilizers, and other substances.
 
• They were most successful in regions with proper irrigation, so the first phase of the Green Revolution focused on states with better infrastructure. 
 
• In the **second phase of the Green Revolution, HYV technology spread to more states and included more types of crops**
